# Testament of Joseph — 11
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The copy of the testament of Joseph. **2** When he was about to die he called his sons and his brothers, and said to them: **3** My brethren and my children, hearken to Joseph the beloved of Israel; give ear, my sons, to your father. **4** I have seen in my life envy and death, yet I went not astray, but persevered in the truth of the Lord. **5** These my brethren hated me, but the Lord loved me: they wished to slay me, but the God of my fathers guarded me: they let me down into a pit, and the Most High brought me up again. **6** I was sold into slavery, and the Lord of all made me free: I was taken into captivity, and his gracious hand succoured me: I was beset with hunger, and the Lord himself nourished me. **7** I was alone, and God comforted me: I was sick, and the Lord visited me: I was in prison, and my God shewed favour unto me: in bonds, and he released me: slandered, and he pleaded my cause: bitterly spoken against by the Egyptians, and he delivered me: envied by my fellow-slaves, and he exalted me.

**2** And this chief captain of Pharaoh entrusted to me his house. **2** And I struggled against a shameless woman, urging me to transgress with her; but the God of Israel my father delivered me from the burning flame. **3** I was cast into prison, I was beaten, I was mocked; and the Lord granted me to find mercy in the sight of the keeper of the prison. **4** For the Lord doth not forsake them that fear him, neither in darkness, nor in bonds, nor in tribulation, nor in necessity. **5** For God is not put to shame as a man, nor as the son of man is he afraid; but in all those places he giveth succour, and in divers ways he comforteth, though for a little space he departeth in order to try the inclination of the soul. **6** In ten temptations he showed me approved, and in all of them I endured; for endurance is a mighty charm, and patience giveth many good things.

**3** How often did the Egyptian woman threaten me with death! **2** How often did she give me over to punishment, and then call me back and threaten me when I would not company with her! **3** She said to me: Thou shalt be lord of me, and all that is in mine house, if thou wilt give thyself to me. **4** And I remembered the words of my father, and going into my chamber, I wept and prayed unto the Lord. **5** And I fasted in those seven years, and I appeared to the Egyptians as one living delicately, for they that fast for God's sake receive beauty of face. **6** And if my lord were absent she would speak to me of sexual sin, and if he were present she would drug his wine and give me to drink of it. **7** And if he were away upon his business she would threaten me with death; and if I would not company with her, she said: I will tell against thee that thou didst assault me. **8** And when she saw that I refused her, she caught hold of my garments.

**4** And when she could not prevail over me, she came to me as a friend, praising my chastity and promising to prevail with her husband for my sake; and when I would not be moved, she said: I will prove my piety in thy behalf by my praise of thee, before the Lord. **2** And I was greatly grieved in my soul, that she should have spoken thus to me; and I remembered that Jacob my father had commanded me to keep myself from all woman who was not his wife. **3** For God loveth him who in a den of wickedness combines fasting with chastity, rather than the man who in kings' chambers liveth delicately without offending. **4** And if a man liveth in chastity and desireth also glory, and the Most High knoweth that it is expedient for him, he bestoweth this also upon him.

**5** How often, though she were sick, did she come down to me at unlooked for times, and listened to my voice as I prayed! **2** And when I heard her groanings I held my peace. **3** For when I was in her house she was wont to bare her arms, and breasts, and legs, that I might lie with her; for she was very beautiful, splendidly adorned in order to beguile me. **4** And the Lord guarded me from her devices.

**6** Ye see therefore, my children, how great things patience worketh, and prayer with fasting. **2** So ye too, if ye follow after chastity and purity with patience and prayer with fasting in humility of heart, the Lord will dwell among you, because he loveth chastity. **3** And wheresoever the Most High dwelleth, even though envy, or slavery, or slander befall a man, the Lord who dwelleth in him, for his sake will not only deliver him from evil, but also exalt and glorify him, even as me. **4** For in every way the man is guarded, whether in deed, or in word, or in thought.

**7** My brethren know how my father loved me, and yet I was not exalted in my heart; although I was a child, I had the fear of God in my heart; for I knew that all things would pass away. **2** I did not raise myself against them with evil, but I honoured my brethren; and out of respect for them, even when they sold me, I refrained from telling the Ishmaelites that I was a son of Jacob, a great man and a mighty. **3** Do ye also, my children, have the fear of God in all your doings, and honour your brethren; for everyone who doeth the law of the Lord shall be loved by him.

**8** And now, my children, observe all that I command you; and give honour to Levi and Judah. **2** For from them shall arise unto you the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world, one who saveth all the Gentiles and Israel. **3** For his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, which shall not pass away; but my kingdom among you shall come to an end as a watcher's hammock, which after the summer is gone is seen no more.

**9** For I know that after my death the Egyptians will afflict you; but God will avenge you, and will bring you into that which he promised to your fathers. **2** But ye shall carry up my bones with you; for when my bones are being taken up thither, the Lord shall be with you in light, and Beliar shall be in darkness with the Egyptians. **3** And carry ye up Asenath your mother to the Hippodrome and bury her near Rachel your mother's mother. **4** And when he had said these things he stretched out his feet and fell asleep in a beautiful and good sleep. **5** And all Israel mourned for him with a great mourning.

---
*End of Testament of Joseph*
